title: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy
desc: Immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis (IEC-EC) is a delayed toxicity of ciltacabtagene autoleucel. The US Multiple Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium retrospectively adjudicated 54 suspected cases from 8 institutions: 41 were IEC-EC (31 confirmed by anti-camelid variable heavy-chain immunohistochemistry, 10 probable). Through September 2025, cumulative incidence was 3.0% (39 of 1,308 ciltacabtagene autoleucel recipients; 95% CI 2.1–4.1%); 12-month competing-risk incidence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.1–4.1%). Median symptom onset was 75 days after infusion. Grade ≥3 diarrhea occurred in 85% (34 of 40 with diarrhea); 73% (30 of 41) required parenteral nutrition. Despite normal upper endoscopy in 41% (9 of 22), duodenal biopsies showed villous blunting, apoptotic bodies and a dense cytotoxic T cell infiltrate, CD4+ in 61% (19 of 31), CD8+ in 26% (8 of 31) and mixed in 13% (4 of 31). A dominant T cell clone was detected in 76% (13 of 17 tested). Delayed neurotoxicity co-occurred in 41% (17 of 41). At last follow-up, 32% (13 of 41) resolved, 27% (11 of 41) had ongoing symptoms and 41% (17 of 41) died with active IEC-EC. Combined biologic and T cell-directed therapy yielded the highest resolution (55%, 6 of 11) in small subgroups. IEC-EC is potentially fatal and requires systematic evaluation and early directed therapy.

title: Metastatic Prostate Cancer Treatment Variation in Veterans.
desc: [JAMA network open] Not all men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) receive the recommended combination therapy of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) and/or chemotherapy. To determine factors associated with combination therapy use among veterans with mCSPC in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) system. This cohort study included US veterans diagnosed with mCSPC between January 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, who were followed up through June 30, 2025. National multicenter data were obtained from the VHA electronic health record, community care settings (private care paid with VHA benefits), and Medicare. All included veterans were identified through a validated natural language processing algorithm, were followed up in the VHA for at least 2 years prior to their metastatic diagnosis, were provided ADT within the first 6 months of diagnosis, and received no prostate cancer-directed therapy in the year prior to diagnosis. Clinical factors (eg, comorbidities, frailty, prostate cancer burden at diagnosis) and nonclinical factors (eg, annual household income, neighborhood disadvantage) were investigated to determine their association with the outcome. The primary outcome was receipt of combination therapy (ie, ADT plus ARPI [abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide] and/or docetaxel) vs ADT alone. Information on these treatments was obtained through pharmacy records. Multilevel logistic regression models were used and marginal predicted probabilities were reported to determine the associations of factors with receipt of combination therapy. Variation among VHA facilities was reported. A total of 4023 veterans (mean [SD] age, 75.3 [8.0] years) met eligibility criteria. Of these patients, 2339 (58.1%) had de novo metastatic disease, while 1684 (41.9%) had recurrent disease. Overall, 2564 patients (63.7%) received combination therapy. In adjusted analyses, older veterans (eg, aged 85-89 years: predicted probability, -14.1 [95% CI, -20.5 to -8.2] percentage points [pp]) and veterans with more comorbidities (eg, congestive heart failure: predicted probability, -7.5 [95% CI, -12.9 to -2.5] pp) were less likely to receive combination therapy. Annual household income and neighborhood disadvantage were not associated with receipt of combination therapy. title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
desc: Artificial intelligence for combinatorial optimization depends on high-quality, structured training data, yet transforming ambiguous natural-language descriptions into precise, executable formal models remains a major bottleneck, traditionally requiring extensive manual effort and domain expertise. We develop CPAM-LLM, an automated constraint-programming modeling framework based on large language models that converts unstructured problem specifications into validated and executable formal models. The framework integrates retrieval-augmented generation grounded in formal concept analysis for structural validation, chaos-mapping-based data augmentation to enhance cross-domain generalization, and dynamic constraint adaptation to accommodate evolving problem settings. We demonstrate its effectiveness across five scenarios, including DNA sequence design, reconfigurable energy storage systems, and unmanned vehicle logistics. The results show that the framework can automate the data-to-model pipeline while adapting reliably to changing requirements, providing a practical approach to automated data formalization and indicating the importance of accessible, high-quality structured data for reliable downstream artificial intelligence applications.

title: Postoperative timing effects on AI-based resection-cavity segmentation in glioma: multi-site evaluation and relevance assessment
desc: Recent evidence underscores the need for early post-surgical cavity delineation to improve brain tumor treatment. Manual segmentation—the gold standard—is slow and labor-intensive but necessary to link early post-surgical lesions to brain connectivity and functional outcome. Using one of the largest post-operative glioma MRI datasets available to date (N = 1056), (i) we evaluated the effect of postoperative scan timing on AI-based resection-cavity segmentation; (ii) we investigated whether automated segmentations replicate findings showing that surgery-induced network disconnection severity predicts worse language fluency scores. While the segmentation of chronic cavities yielded accurate results, early postoperative segmentations initially posed challenges due to domain shift. Semi-supervised learning and model fine-tuning overcame this issue, providing preliminary evidence supporting the adoption of AI-driven disconnectomics. We provide a robust AI-driven tool for early postsurgical assessment and functional recovery prediction in neuro-oncological care, showing that the time between surgery and cavity delineation is critical for AI reliability.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
desc: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases. Existing models often satisfy one requirement while failing the other, and training only for safety or personalization leaves a gap in joint success. We therefore propose PReMind, a two-phase reinforcement learning framework that combines on-demand and forced-call interactions (memory always retrieved) to jointly train grounded memory use and hazard response. At 4B, PReMind raises joint success from 12.9% to 28.6% over its base on the interdependency set and improves hazard adequacy and correct abstention on the main test. Joint-success gains persist under forced-call evaluation and under a second LLM judge across three Phase II seeds; averaged over these seeds, joint success also improves on unseen hazard groups. These findings highlight the need to evaluate and train personal assistants to connect visual evidence with the relevant person's context.

title: NativeSeg: Native Vision Language Segmentation of 3D Computed Tomography via Spatial Visual Tokens and Verified Local Zoom
desc: Text prompted 3D computed tomography (CT) segmentation requires both full slice context and fine boundary precision across volumes where over $80\%$ of organ prompted slices lack the queried target. Existing medical vision language models (VLMs) are largely non native segmenters: they delegate pixel delineation outside the VLM by compressing reasoning into a 1D [SEG] vector for an external Segment Anything Model (SAM) decoder, quantizing masks into lossy discrete codebooks, or issuing box prompts to stateless external SAM tools without empty slice screening or spatial state memory. We introduce NativeSeg, a native vision language segmentation framework on Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapted Qwen3.8-27B that performs dense mask decoding, volumetric triage, spatial error self diagnosis, and multiround local zoom directly over the VLM's 2D spatial visual tokens without external SAM decoders. NativeSeg decodes confidence maps from upper layer 2D spatial tokens fused with a five slice U-Net pathway, halts at zero zooms on $>91\%$ of standalone evaluations via a native presence gate ( ), localizes uncertain boundaries via a 20 cell multiscale error gate ( ), and accepts zoomed updates only when predicted error decreases. Trained solely on adult CT, NativeSeg improves Round $0$ DSC by $+19.81$ and $+7.04$ points over discrete codebook and 1D [SEG] readouts on the identical backbone, reaches $86.81\%$ adult and $87.04\%$ zero shot pediatric DSC, and safely refines 2D nnU-Net ($89.52\%$ adult; $86.86\%$ pediatric), 3D SegVol ($86.81\%$), and 3D VoxTell ($89.85\%$).

title: Sparrowhawk: harnessing WebAssembly for private microbial genomics, and beyond
desc: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. Producing such an application which implements a new algorithm, even though it would access a much wider audience, is typically beyond the expertise and time constraints of computational method developers. Here, we show our Sparrowhawk framework can rapidly create an interactive web application to run interactive analysis on a user's machine, across a wide range of algorithms. Focusing first on genomic epidemiology, a domain with a specific need for such methods, we created novel lightweight methods for genome assembly, antimicrobial resistance gene annotation, and taxonomic identification. Our results exceed performance of previous lightweight methods, and produce results that reproduce or closely match previous analysis pipelines. By using WebAssembly, our framework benefits from not requiring installation, command line knowledge, or transferring sensitive data over an internet connection. We show how algorithms from other researchers, and spanning fields from machine learning to physics, can rapidly be ported to web tools using our framework. We demonstrate an immediate impact on microbial bioinformatics, but expect that uptake of Sparrowhawk by developers of other tools broadly will help other researchers, and create new tools for teaching and public engagement. Thanks to the broad availability and familiarity with web browser tools across society, Sparrowhawk has the potential to significantly lower the barrier to entry to advanced computational methods.

title: Bridging Brain Connectome and Clinical Notes: A Novel Multimodal Framework for MCI Study.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
desc: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] Integrating brain imaging data with clinical reports enables the effective use of complementary multimodal information, supporting more accurate and timely diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. This approach has gained growing attention in brain disorder research, yet significant limitations remain: how to encode brain structure and function to reflect meaningful neurological patterns, and how to effectively link objective imaging data with subjective text-based reports while establishing interpretable associations. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal framework that aligns brain connectomes with clinical reports in a shared cross-modal latent space at both subject and connectome levels. Our key innovation lies in treating brain subnetworks as tokens rather than raw image patches, enabling more efficient identification of system-level associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical observations. These cross-modal associations are further fused to enhance mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prediction and provide interpretable diagnostic insights. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to integrate both structural and functional brain connectivity with non-imaging clinical information. Experimental validation on the ADNI dataset demonstrates performance competitive with recently reported methods. Notably, despite no explicit connectome-token-level supervision, the learned connectome-text associations recover multiple relationships independently reported in the neuroimaging and clinical literature, suggesting that the framework captures clinically coherent cross-modal associations. This pioneering work advances multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis by bridging the gap between neuroimaging analysis and clinical text interpretation through innovative connectome tokenization and cross-modal alignment strategies.

title: AI-Assisted Diagnosis: Big Data Analytics in Clinical Decision Support.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), AI-assisted clinical diagnosis, driven by big data analytics and machine/deep learning (ML/DL), has brought great changes in clinical decision. AI enhances disease detection, classification, and treatment planning by processing diverse data such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical images, and genomics. Key applications include high-accuracy cancer screening, neurological disorder prediction, and diagnostics in ophthalmology, endocrinology, and pediatrics. Significant challenges involve data quality/standardization, model interpretability, and ethical/legal concerns. Mitigation strategies include federated learning, Explainable AI, and fairness constraints. Future directions focus on multimodal data fusion, real-time monitoring via wearables, and collaborative human-AI diagnostics. AI is positioned as a tool to augment clinicians, promising improved diagnostic precision, efficiency, and accessibility in precision medicine, contingent on overcoming technical and ethical hurdles through interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
desc: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning. We evaluate our methods on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and knowledge unlearning. For mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approaches achieve competitive downstream performance while better preserving general capabilities, offering a favorable acquisition--retention trade-off relative to the baselines. For knowledge unlearning, our main results on TOFU and MUSE show a better balance between targeted forgetting and knowledge retention than the baselines, with retention performance close to the from-scratch retraining reference.

title: Localizing Unsampled Regions in Partially Sampled Pathogen Phylogenies Using Machine Learning
desc: Motivation: Pathogen phylogenies are useful for monitoring the evolution of pathogens and for detecting new variants, as it provides information that can aid public health decisions and outbreak response. Since not all infections are sequenced, certain pathogen lineages may be missing or only poorly represented in reconstructed phylogenies. Identifying these gaps could help to determine where additional data collection is required. Results: We developed a computational method to locate regions of missing samples from the observed tree alone, without sequences from those samples. A machine learning model predicts which branches lead toward the missing region. Beam search then identifies three representative paths and estimates a candidate most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of the missing region for each path. We tested this framework on 5,000 simulated phylogenies where we controlled which tips were deleted. On an independent test set, the best candidate recovered an average of 89.9% of deleted tips, increasing to 90.7% when all three candidates were combined. Predicted and true MRCAs lay on the same ancestral-descendant lineage in 91.3% of cases. We further evaluated the approach on an empirical SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny with introduced missingness. By identifying potentially underrepresented lineages, this framework could help real-time identification of missing infections and improve outbreak response.

Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR + T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy
desc: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid cancer.
desc: [Frontiers in endocrinology] Thyroid cancer is one of the most common endocrine malignancies, and its rising incidence has increased the demand for more accurate and efficient diagnostic and management strategies. Current clinical management mainly relies on ultrasonography, fine-needle aspiration (FNA), surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression, and systemic treatment in selected advanced cases. However, substantial interobserver variability, indeterminate cytology, and heterogeneity in tumor behavior still complicate diagnosis and risk stratification. In thyroid cancer, AI(Artificial intelligence) -assisted models have been applied to ultrasound, CT, MRI, cytology, histopathology, and genomic data, with promising performance in distinguishing benign from malignant nodules, predicting lymph node metastasis and key mutations, and supporting individualized management. This review critically synthesizes evidence across these applications, focusing on study design, validation strategies, generalizability, and clinical relevance. It also examines explainable AI, emerging foundation models, and regulatory and implementation challenges. Although many models report high diagnostic or predictive performance, these results alone do not establish improvements in clinical decision-making or patient outcomes. Prospective clinical validation, cost-effectiveness assessment, and evaluation of integration into clinical workflows are needed to determine whether AI provides meaningful benefits over standard care.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Raman Spectroscopy for Quantitative Prediction of Multicomponent Mixtures
desc: Machine Learning (ML)-assisted Raman spectroscopy that can efficiently analyze molecularly specific fingerprints is well suited for quantitative analysis of complex chemical mixtures. However, developing accurate predictive ML models for multicomponent systems remains difficult because collecting sufficient experimental calibration data is slow, expensive, and limited. In this work, we present a ML-assisted Raman spectroscopy framework for predicting the quantitative composition of multicomponent lipid mixtures (consisting of 15 lipids). To reduce the experimental burden of generating extensive multicomponent spectral datasets, we computationally constructed a large spectral library using experimentally measured pure-component Raman spectra from 15 lipids, including triglycerides, medium- and long-chain fatty acids, and fatty acid methyl and ethyl esters. Mixture compositions were sampled across a constrained compositional space and used to generate training spectra from weighted combinations of the pure component spectra. Experimentally prepared mixtures were then used to evaluate the model under real measurement conditions. To reduce the mismatch between library-generated spectra and experimental mixture spectra, a linear correction strategy was applied to account for systematic spectral differences caused by mixing effects, intermolecular interactions, and measurement variability. The corrected experimental spectra were then used for concentration prediction with an uncertainty-aware workflow. The compositions of the 15 lipid mixtures were successfully predicted using the ML model trained solely on a simulated dataset, achieving R^2 values exceeding 0.95 for each lipid. By combining scalable, library-based model training with experimental validation on physical multicomponent mixtures, this approach minimizes the need for exhaustive calibration datasets while maintaining high quantitative accuracy. The proposed framework offers a practical path for quantitative Raman analysis of chemical mixtures and can easily be extended to quality control applications across the food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and chemical industries.

title: Analyzing Electronic Health Records for Precision Medicine.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Precision medicine relies heavily on electronic health records (EHRs) to systematically capture longitudinal clinical data across populations. Integrating omics data, such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, with EHRs holds transformative potential for individual-level disease risk assessment and therapeutic optimization. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly multimodal learning algorithms, have enabled deeper exploration of EHR data, enhancing predictive modeling, patient stratification, and phenotyping. These artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches are expanding the scope of precision medicine from research contexts to scalable, real-time clinical decision-making. In real-world implementation, however, leveraging EHRs for precision medicine demands navigating complex technical, ethical, and operational challenges. These include data interoperability, model generalizability, and equity concerns. Future efforts should emphasize standardization, responsible AI practices, and integration of digital health and patient-reported outcomes to build learning health systems that are adaptive, equitable, and clinically impactful.

source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] As a crucial component in preclinical cancer research, patient-derived models (PDMs) are experiencing a substantial transformation due to AI integration. AI improves the conversion efficiency of PDMs' static-dynamic predictions through cross-modal data integration and supports a comprehensive precision medicine technology platform that encompasses everything from molecular mechanisms to clinical translation. In clinical translation, the "AI-PDMs" system is revolutionizing oncology drug development and enabling personalized treatment decisions, moving from experience-based methods to data-driven strategies. This paper provides a detailed summary of AI's innovative uses of PDMs, such as machine learning-based high-dimensional pharmacological sensitivity data mining, deep learning-enhanced 3D tumor microenvironment modeling, and computer vision-driven advancements in pathological feature annotation, thereby offering a systematic framework for future cancer diagnosis and treatment innovations.

InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on bio-medical engineering
desc: [IEEE transactions on bio-medical engineering] To develop and validate InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular data and longitudinal EHR trajectories for critically ill patients requiring mechanical ventilation and venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), enabling scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in high-risk cohorts. InterGenEHR+ uses an optional large language model (LLM) parser for text-driven input. For single-time-point generation, we integrate variational autoencoders (VAEs) and diffusion models conditioned on observed variables. Multiple diffusion architectures support conditional longitudinal generation. The framework is evaluated on a multi-institutional VV-ECMO cohort of 874 patients using distributional fidelity metrics, imputation accuracy, adherence to clinical constraints, downstream mortality prediction tasks, and clinician evaluation. Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the best performance in parsing clinician prompts while maintaining a low spurious slot rate. The experimental results demonstrate strengths across IGE variants: IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE show strong performance in single-time-point generation, whereas IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI achieve the best performance on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. In downstream evaluations across five random seeds and three classifiers, models trained on synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings further indicate that the generated trajectories are clinically plausible and consistent with the requested scenarios. InterGenEHR+ enables clinician-specified conditional generation of clinically coherent EHR trajectories with strong statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort and could be extended to other clinical settings. This framework supports the development and evaluation of machine learning systems in data-sparse critical care settings and advances clinically grounded synthetic data generation for biomedical research.1.

Future Directions for Precision Medicine in the Age of AI.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Precision medicine, which involves tailoring medical treatment to the individual characteristics of each patient, is poised for a new era of advancement through artificial intelligence (AI). This chapter explores the future directions of precision medicine in the context of AI-driven innovation, focusing on emerging technologies and their impact on personalized care. We discuss recent breakthroughs in AI-enabled diagnostics, genomics, drug discovery, and clinical decision-making, highlighting how these developments are reshaping the practice of medicine. We also examine the challenges and opportunities in implementing AI for precision medicine, including data integration, model interpretability, regulatory considerations, and ethical issues. Drawing on high-impact research and reports from leading institutions, we present a forward-looking analysis of how AI will drive the next generation of personalized treatments. The convergence of AI and precision medicine promises to revolutionize healthcare by improving early disease detection, optimizing therapy selection, and enabling truly individualized patient care.

Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.
desc: [Current opinion in ophthalmology] This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone. AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.

title: AI医疗诊断正在上海加速落地 政策与实践双驱动
Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials. In precision oncology, MDTs can simulate disease progression and therapeutic responses, allowing treatment regimens to be tested virtually before administration and thereby supporting personalized treatment decisions. In virtual clinical trials, MDTs can enhance randomized trials through the PROCOVA™ methodology, provide synthetic control arms for single-arm studies, and support the identification of optimal dosing regimens in early-phase trials. However, MDTs also face challenges related to computational complexity, generalizability across diverse populations, AI-related model validation and regulatory compliance, and underdeveloped ethical frameworks for continuous-learning systems. Despite these challenges, MDTs hold considerable potential to reshape cancer care, optimize individualized therapies, and accelerate oncology drug development.

title: Artificial intelligence in monitoring noninvasive ventilation and high-flow nasal therapy: current knowledge and future expectations.
source: PubMed · European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
desc: [European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society] Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and high-flow nasal therapy (HFNT) are central to the management of acute and chronic respiratory failure, yet their monitoring remains largely descriptive and reactive. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform this paradigm by enabling dynamic, predictive and individualised approaches to respiratory support. This narrative review summarises current knowledge and future perspectives of AI applications in NIV and HFNT monitoring. AI techniques, including supervised and unsupervised machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid approaches, can integrate multimodal data across different timescales, from high-frequency ventilator signals to longitudinal telemonitoring data. Current applications include early detection of treatment failure, outcome prediction, patient phenotyping and automated detection of patient-ventilator asynchrony. While these approaches have shown promising performance in retrospective and proof-of-concept studies, their implementation in routine clinical practice remains limited. Key challenges include data heterogeneity, limited sample sizes, insufficient external validation and issues related to interpretability and integration into clinical workflows. Regulatory and ethical considerations further highlight the need to ensure transparency, safety and clinician trust. Future developments are expected to move towards adaptive and closed-loop systems capable of continuously optimising respiratory support. Ultimately, AI should be viewed as a tool to augment clinical expertise, supporting a shift towards more anticipatory, personalised and responsive respiratory care.

title: Pharmacometrics, Artificial Intelligence, and Machine Learning in Precision Dosing and Clinical Toxicology.
desc: [Therapeutic drug monitoring] Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) enables individualized pharmacotherapy for drugs with high interpatient variability and concentration-dependent effects. Conventional Bayesian approaches, although clinically established, may not fully capture pharmacokinetic complexity in dynamic or heterogeneous patient populations. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning methods offer complementary capabilities, including modeling nonlinear relationships and integrating high-dimensional clinical data. Peer-reviewed studies that applied AI or machine-learning methods to TDM between January 2017 and April 2026 were reviewed in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Studies involving adult and pediatric populations were included, whereas reviews, editorials, and animal studies were excluded. Forty-seven studies covering a range of drugs, including vancomycin, tacrolimus, antiepileptics, mycophenolic acid, methotrexate, and voriconazole, were included. Tree-based ensemble methods, particularly eXtreme Gradient Boosting, random forest, and gradient boosting, were the most frequently applied algorithms. In general, these methods demonstrated strong predictive performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values up to 0.90 for classification tasks and coefficient of determination values up to 0.85 for regression tasks. In 13 studies, AI models demonstrated predictive performance comparable with or exceeding that of traditional population pharmacokinetic and Bayesian approaches for selected applications. However, these comparisons were heterogeneous and often based on retrospective data sets with limited external validation. AI-based methods have considerable potential for enhancing TDM, particularly for dose optimization, drug-exposure estimation, and toxicity prediction. However, evidence linking improved predictive performance to meaningful clinical outcomes remains limited.

title: Calibrating trust in generative artificial intelligence for clinical communication through Chinese medical humanism.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Generative artificial intelligence is entering clinical communication through patient messaging, health education, and conversational decision support. Its capacity to produce reassuring language can coexist with inaccurate advice, unclear responsibility, and culturally inappropriate explanations. This mini-review examines how Chinese medical humanism can inform the calibration of trust in these encounters. Targeted literature identification integrates studies of trust and perceived empathy, research on traditional Chinese medicine communication, and medical education evidence with normative scholarship. The evidence distinguishes perceived empathy from relational accountability and technical performance from demonstrated patient benefit. Chinese medical ideals of benevolence, sincerity, holistic attention, and contextual judgment offer resources for interpreting professional responsibilities, but their incorporation into artificial intelligence has not been shown to restore trust or improve health outcomes. We synthesize these insights into a proposed dual-verification approach: an epistemic track checks evidence, uncertainty, and safety, while a relational track checks patient understanding, cultural meaning, preferences, and access to human care. Their convergence supports accountable communication and allows unresolved concerns to trigger human review. Educational applications connect critical appraisal of generated responses with reflection on classical medical ethics. Evaluation should prioritize appropriate reliance, error recognition, patient agency, and equitable access rather than maximizing trust scores. This approach reframes humanistic integration as a set of responsibilities for clinicians and institutions, with its effectiveness remaining an empirical question.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Precision Nutrition: From Multi-Omics Integration to Personalized Dietary Interventions.
desc: [Clinical nutrition ESPEN] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being investigated as a tool for precision nutrition because it can analyse heterogeneous dietary, clinical, physiological, behavioural, and molecular data. This narrative review critically examines how machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, explainable AI, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable technologies, and multi-omics approaches may support individualized nutritional assessment and decision-making. Particular attention is given to the distinction between predictive research, digital personalized nutrition, AI-enabled clinical interventions, and commercial nutrition platforms. Current evidence shows that personalized digital nutrition can improve selected dietary behaviours, while observational AI and multi-omics studies can predict substantial inter-individual variation in metabolic responses. Importantly, evidence that an AI-enabled intervention improves clinical outcomes is still limited and is concentrated in selected settings, including a multicentre randomized trial of an AI-based dietary management platform in adults with type 2 diabetes. Emerging technologies such as large language models, digital twins, federated learning, and adaptive algorithms remain promising but require prospective clinical validation. Major barriers include data quality, algorithmic bias, privacy, interoperability, model transparency, regulatory uncertainty, and limited external validation. Future research should prioritize pragmatic multicentre randomized trials, transparent reporting of model performance, independent validation, health-economic evaluation, and clinically meaningful outcomes. AI should therefore be considered an adjunct to evidence-based nutritional care rather than a replacement for professional clinical judgement. The review differs from technology-centred and methodology-focused reviews by explicitly linking AI modalities and multi-omics data with evidence maturity, clinical trial findings, implementation barriers, and the level of inference justified for each technology.

title: Multimodal deep learning approach for frailty classification using electrocardiogram and chest X-ray imaging.
desc: [PLOS digital health] Frailty is a critical age-related syndrome associated with increased risks of disability, hospitalization, and mortality. While Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) is the standard for evaluation, it is often subjective, time-consuming, and resource-intensive. To address these limitations, this study developed and validated a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates chest X-rays (CXR) and electrocardiograms (ECG) to provide an objective and rapid tool for frailty classification. We retrospectively analyzed data from 2,830 older adults who underwent CGA between 2007 and 2024, partitioned chronologically into training, validation, and test sets. Frailty was defined using a Multidimensional Frailty Score (MFS) > 5. Three deep learning models were trained and evaluated: a CXR-only model (EVA-X vision transformer), an ECG-only model (DenseNet-121), and a multimodal model combining both inputs. The multimodal model outperformed the single-modality models and four non-imaging clinical baseline models incorporating age, sex, comorbidity index, or routine laboratory variables, achieving the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.778 and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.726. For continuous MFS estimation, the multimodal model achieved the highest Pearson correlation (r = 0.610) and the lowest mean absolute error (MAE = 1.68) among the evaluated models. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was used to qualitatively explore the image regions that influenced model predictions. This multimodal AI framework demonstrates modest classification performance and feasibility for frailty screening. By leveraging routinely collected clinical images, this framework may serve as a practical screening adjunct to identify older adults who may benefit from formal CGA. Further studies are needed to determine its clinical utility when applied preoperatively for the stratification of postoperative risk.

title: Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research.
desc: [Biomedicine & pharmacotherapy = Biomedecine & pharmacotherapie] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in cardiovascular research where conventional analysis struggles with scale, heterogeneity, and multimodal integration. Its contribution differs across imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. This narrative review examines substantive applications of machine learning and deep learning while distinguishing them from routine bioinformatics and purely biophysical modeling. We assess independent biological units, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies. Deep-learning imaging systems can provide reproducible quantitative phenotypes, but workflow performance alone does not establish mechanism. In single-cell and spatial studies, clustering, integration, trajectory inference, and network reconstruction generally yield associations or hypotheses unless experimentally supported. Mechanistic interpretation is bounded by the specific effect established through targeted perturbation or rescue with functional testing; lineage tracing and orthogonal readouts provide complementary support, not standalone proof of causation. Hybrid AI-biophysical models may accelerate personalized simulation, whereas heart-on-chip, engineered tissue, and organoid systems without learned components are validation platforms rather than AI methods. In drug discovery, active learning and molecular redesign can prioritize candidates, but predicted reductions in ion-channel liability do not demonstrate biological safety or reduced proarrhythmic risk. Major limitations include pseudoreplication, data leakage, domain shift, batch effects, uncertain labels, few independent hearts, demographic imbalance, incomplete calibration, and limited transfer among animal, iPSC-derived, and adult human systems. AI is most valuable when it produces robust phenotypes or experimentally testable hypotheses within a transparent validation framework, rather than when predictive accuracy is treated as mechanistic evidence.

title: AI-Driven Monitoring of Biomechanical Loading in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is difficult to identify rapidly because clinical symptoms may be delayed and conventional CT or MRI often reveals no structural abnormalities. Biomechanics-based monitoring provides an objective complementary strategy by measuring head kinematics at the moment of impact and estimating the resulting brain deformation. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI) can overcome two major barriers to this approach: errors in wearable-sensor measurements and the high computational cost of finite element head models. AI-based methods can denoise instrumented mouthguard signals, distinguish true impacts from false triggers, and infer impact direction, location, speed, and force. Deep learning head models can further map six-degree-of-freedom head kinematics to whole-brain strain and strain-rate distributions within milliseconds, enabling near-real-time tissue-level injury assessment. Recent advances, including kinematic feature optimization, principal component analysis, impact subtyping, transfer learning, unsupervised domain adaptation, and spatiotemporal prediction, have improved model efficiency, interpretability, and generalizability across impact scenarios. Integrating wearable sensing with AI-accelerated brain modeling could support rapid removal from exposure, earlier clinical evaluation and intervention, and monitoring of cumulative impact dose. Future research should improve sensor wearability and coupling, incorporate subject-specific brain morphology and cortical folding, represent cerebrospinal fluid mechanics more realistically, and develop unified models that jointly estimate brain deformation and predict clinically confirmed injury. AI-enabled biomechanical monitoring may therefore complement symptom- and imaging-based assessments and advance real-time, personalized mTBI detection and prevention.

title: Deep Learning Assisted Label-Free Microscopy for Cell Death Analysis in Real-Time.
desc: [Journal of biophotonics] Cytotoxicity assessment is fundamental to many areas of biomedical research, yet cell viability assays alone do not reveal death mechanisms, for example, apoptosis and necrosis. Conventional endpoint assays, including Western blotting, ELISA, and fluorescence microscopy/cytometry, require costly reagents, extensive sample preparation, and specialized expertise, limiting accessibility and scalability. Here, we present a multimodal spatiotemporal deep learning framework for classifying cell death mechanisms from phase-contrast and dark-field microscopy. Time-lapse videos of drug-treated BT-20 breast cancer cells were recorded in both modalities. These cells were used to train 3D convolutional, convolutional-recurrent, transfer-learning, and transformer models. Combined across architectures and modalities, the models achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.98 on recordings not used for training. The CytoMorpheus Analyzer runs the full pipeline from raw microscopy data, classifying over a thousand cells within minutes. These results highlight the potential of label-free microscopy with deep learning for real-time, high-throughput profiling of cell death and drug response.

title: Statistical Design, Inference, and Trustworthy Medical AI.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] In the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence (AI), statistics plays a crucial role in addressing challenges faced by medical AI. This review begins by highlighting the primary tasks of medical AI and the integration of statistical methodologies into their modeling processes. Despite the widespread application of AI in medicine and healthcare, key challenges persist: poor model interpretability, lack of causal reasoning, overfitting, unfairness, imbalanced datasets, AI "hallucinations" and "disinformation." Statistics provides unique strategies to tackle these challenges, including rigorous statistical design, regularization techniques, and statistical frameworks grounded in causal inference. Finally, the review offers several recommendations for the sustainable development of medical AI: enhancing data quality, promoting model simplicity and transparency, fostering independent validation standards, and facilitating interdisciplinary collaboration between statisticians and medical AI practitioners.

title: Novel Breath Segmentation and Predictive Quality Classification Model for Pediatric Bag-Mask Ventilation Using Capnography Waveforms.
desc: [Critical care explorations] Bag-mask ventilation (BMV) is a critical phase of pediatric airway management, yet objective feedback remains limited. To develop and validate a two-stage, CO2-only framework for pediatric BMV assessment comprising automated breath segmentation and machine learning classification of breaths according to predefined low-quality criteria for insufficient ventilation. We hypothesized that our model would achieve area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) greater than or equal to 0.75 and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) greater than or equal to 0.75. We retrospectively analyzed capnography waveforms from 85 critically ill children receiving peri-intubation BMV in a quaternary-care PICU. Flow and pressure data established reference-standard low-quality criteria: expiratory tidal volume (VTE) less than 4 mL/kg of ideal body weight, mask leak greater than 40%, or upper airway obstruction (VTE 30 cm H2O and leak > 80%). CO2-based segmentation was validated in 10 randomly selected patients comprising 605 manually adjudicated breaths. Classification performance was internally validated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation within the derivation cohort; no independent validation cohort was used. A rule-based algorithm segmented continuous CO2 waveforms into breaths. Deep learning architectures then used CO2 waveforms alone to classify breaths according to whether they met predefined low-quality criteria. The CO2-only algorithm identified 6942 breaths (median, 66 per patient [interquartile range, 47-100 per patient]); 49.5% met at least one low-quality criterion. Segmentation achieved positive predictive value 0.95 (95% CI, 0.93-0.96) and sensitivity 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89). Twenty-seven breaths were adjudicated as false-positive detections (0.05; 95% CI, 0.036-0.074). CO2-only segmentation may miss ventilatory attempts with minimal or absent exhaled CO2. The best-performing classification model achieved AUROC 0.79 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89) and AUPRC 0.75 (95% CI, 0.57-0.88). A CO2-only framework showed proof-of-concept feasibility for breath segmentation and quality classification during pediatric BMV, supporting further development of objective bedside feedback systems.

title: Explainable volumetric deep learning from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI for preoperative IDH prediction in adult-type diffuse gliomas: a two-center study.
desc: [Frontiers in neurology] To evaluate contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1WI) models for preoperative prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status in adult-type diffuse gliomas and explore phenotype associations of influential latent features. This retrospective study included 462 patients. Center 1 provided training (n = 259) and internal-test (n = 65) cohorts, and Center 2 provided external validation (n = 138). Five input-architecture combinations and six classifiers were evaluated against an interpretable logistic benchmark combining age and Visually Accessible Rembrandt Images (VASARI) descriptors. For each architecture, the classifier with the highest observed external area under the curve (AUC) was selected for reporting. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curves, and 100 downstream refits with fixed deep features. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and phenotype association analyses examined influential latent features and their relationships with clinical and imaging phenotypes. Region-of-interest (ROI)-constrained three-dimensional vision Transformer (3D ViT) with a support vector machine (SVM) achieved an external AUC of 0.929 (95% CI, 0.885-0.973), accuracy of 0.848, sensitivity of 0.838, specificity of 0.857, and Brier score of 0.106. The age-VASARI benchmark achieved an external AUC of 0.782. Across downstream refits, the ROI-constrained model had a mean external AUC of 0.930 and the smallest mean training-minus-external AUC difference (0.019). The same 10 features formed the highest-importance SHAP set across cohorts, with different rank orders. Feature_546 correlated with age (r = 0.461), postoperative Ki-67 (r = 0.562), and enhancement quality (r = 0.678; all adjusted p < 0.001). ROI-constrained volumetric learning from CE-T1WI showed promising cross-center IDH discrimination using one routine MRI sequence. Influential latent features were associated with postoperative Ki-67 and recognizable imaging phenotypes. SHAP attribution and these exploratory associations provide complementary perspectives on model behavior in preoperative IDH assessment.

title: AI-empowered lipidomics advances metabolic research.
source: PubMed · Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM
desc: [Trends in endocrinology and metabolism: TEM] The complex structures and dynamic processes of lipids make it challenging to decipher lipid reprogramming in metabolic diseases. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with lipidomics, mass spectrometry imaging, and lipid metabolic fluxomics enables rapid, high-precision, and in-depth spatiotemporal profiling of lipid species. In this review, we summarize advances in AI-empowered lipidomics, which not only accelerate spatiotemporal data processing but also offer new avenues to resolve the heterogeneity of lipid metabolism. Importantly, AI-assisted lipidomics could identify candidate biomarkers and generate testable hypotheses about disease mechanisms. Furthermore, we evaluate whether computational advances yield trustworthy evidence by examining annotation confidence, quantitative accuracy, cross-platform reproducibility, uncertainty calibration, and external validation. We also address the current limitations of AI-assisted lipidomics, particularly the risk of AI hallucinations.

title: The scientific record is never finished.
desc: [Science (New York, N.Y.)] The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Prediction of Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Human-Virus Protein-Protein Interactions (HV-PPIs) are the core mechanisms underlying viral invasion of host cells, completion of the viral life cycle, and induction of pathological responses. Predicting HV-PPIs in higher accuracy is of great significance for elucidating viral pathogenic mechanisms, developing antiviral drugs, and designing vaccines. However, traditional experimental methods such as Yeast Two-Hybrid (Y2H) and Affinity Purification-Mass Spectrometry (AP-MS) face bottlenecks including low throughput, high cost, high false positive rates, and incomplete data in the identification of cross-species interactions. In recent years, computational biology approaches, especially deep learning-based multimodal fusion frameworks, have emerged as the primary driving force for accelerating HV-PPIs prediction. This review systematically summarizes the latest advances in the field of HV-PPIs prediction, elaborates on key aspects such as data construction, feature engineering, deep learning architectures, and performance evaluation, summarizes the technical essentials, advantages, and limitations of existing methods, discusses the development trends of the field by integrating representative research findings from recent years, and serves as a reference for future investigations in this domain.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design Optimization of a Polymeric Membrane Dressing Material Thickness for Prophylactic Efficacy.
desc: [International wound journal] We examined the impact of a polymeric membrane dressing thickness on its prophylactic efficacy for preventing heel pressure injuries, with the aim of identifying an optimal balance between tissue protection and conformability. An innovative framework was applied that integrated artificial intelligence (AI) predictive analysis with biomechanical finite element (FE) modelling. Two AI approaches were used: (i) interactive dialogue to validate reasoning, and (ii) repeated statistical queries to assess prediction consistency. Both a general-purpose AI model and a fine-tuned domain-specific model were tested, showing convergence toward an optimal dressing thickness of 3 to 5 mm. To validate these AI predictions, FE simulations were conducted for dressings of 3, 4 and 5 mm thickness under combined compressive and shear loading of the heel in a supine position. Protective efficacy was quantified using the protective efficacy index, whereas conformability was assessed through bending stiffness. The results indicated that thicker dressing improves tissue protection but reduces flexibility, as could be expected, and importantly, the AI-FE methodology was powerful in supporting the design process. Specifically, among the tested options, the 4 mm thickness provided the most favourable trade-off, offering substantially greater protection than 3 mm while retaining higher conformability than 5 mm. This thickness also aligned with the most frequent AI-generated prediction, reinforcing confidence in the integrated AI-FE workflow. Overall, we demonstrated the potential of AI-assisted design to streamline wound care research and development processes by narrowing design parameter ranges, reducing the reliance on trial-and-error testing and hence lowering the development costs.

title: Technology-Enabled Skin Longevity Optimization.
desc: [Facial plastic surgery : FPS] Aims and Backgrounds: Facial aging is a multifactorial process involving cellular senescence, ultraviolet damage, and structural decline across the epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous fat, and superficial musculoaponeurotic system. Contemporary rejuvenation has evolved beyond surgical repositioning toward biologically targeted cutaneous optimization. Energy-based technologies including laser photothermolysis, radiofrequency-mediated dermal thermomodulation, microfocused ultrasound, and emerging microwave and cryobiologic modalities induce controlled tissue injury that activates wound-healing pathways, fibroblast proliferation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Regenerative strategies including microneedling-assisted mechanotransduction, platelet-derived biologics, autologous fat grafting, collagen biostimulators, and extracellular vesicle therapies provide biologically oriented tissue restoration through paracrine signaling and matrix synthesis. Current and Future Development: Artificial intelligence applications in facial phenotyping, treatment planning, and outcome assessment are emerging. Future directions include senescence-targeting therapies and precision-based multimodal protocols. Multimodal treatment sequencing addressing multiple anatomical layers represents the contemporary standard. Integration of device-based technologies with regenerative adjuncts enables biologically informed, individualized facial rejuvenation.

title: Annual high-resolution mapping reveals warming-driven carbon losses in Spanish forests.
source: PubMed · Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America
desc: [Ecological applications : a publication of the Ecological Society of America] Forests play a crucial role as carbon sinks and are central to climate mitigation strategies, yet their long-term provision of this ecosystem service is increasingly uncertain under climate change. Using deep learning techniques on a multisource dataset-combining multispectral satellite data, airborne laser scanning, and ground-based measurements-we produced 10 m resolution annual maps of live woody carbon stocks in mainland Spain from 2017 to 2024. Our analysis revealed substantial live forest carbon losses: Live woody carbon stocks declined by approximately 19% between 2017 and 2024, with the sharpest decline occurring during 2021-2023 following a severe drought in 2022. These losses signal reduced uptake capacity and increased vulnerability to future carbon emissions through decomposition or fire. Conifer forests and Eucalyptus plantations experienced the greatest relative carbon losses, 31% and 37% respectively, while Quercus spp. forests showed high resistance (3% decline) and low-density woodlands and agroforestry systems were the least affected, with live woody carbon stocks declining only approximately 1% in these areas. Our results are consistent with structural overshoot dynamics, where periods of favorable growing conditions promote vegetation growth that subsequently becomes vulnerable during drier conditions. Specifically, high rainfall and cooler summer temperatures were strongly correlated with subsequent carbon losses. These findings reveal a critical challenge for climate policy as forest mitigation potential is hampered by climate change impacts, especially in Mediterranean regions where drought duration and intensity is increasing. This highlights the urgent need to align adaptation and mitigation policies to enhance forest resilience, carbon stock stability, and long-term climate mitigation capacity.

title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics.
desc: [Science advances] Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

title: Development of a deep learning model to automatically localize anatomic landmarks important for intraperitoneal free fluid detection during focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST).
desc: [PloS one] The Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) exam allows clinicians to rapidly identify intraperitoneal free fluid (FF), which can accumulate in several discrete anatomic locations. These locations represent potential spaces and are defined by adjacent key organ features. Satisfactory evaluation of these organ features is necessary to obtain a complete FAST exam. We sought to develop an algorithm that accurately identified relevant organs important for the FAST exam. Data was used from 218 prospectively enrolled subjects with positive and negative FAST exams yielding 2,218 videos and 323,304 frames. Images were frame annotated for the presence of the following key organ features: liver, caudal liver tip, spleen, caudal spleen tip, kidney, diaphragm, and bladder. Data were randomly split into training, validation, and test sets in a 6:2:2 ratio for training a deep learning model using the YOLOv5 object detection algorithm. Diagnostic accuracy of the test set is reported at the frame and video levels. At the frame level, the mean average precision (mAP50) was 0.71. At the video level, the mean F1 score for organ detection was 0.85. Video level detection of anatomic locations (defined by the co-incidence of two relevant organ structures) of potential FF accumulation showed a mean F1 of 0.79. At the video level, the model was optimized to favor a higher mean specificity (0.90, 95% CI 0.89-0.92) at the expense of a slightly reduced mean sensitivity (0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.90). The inference speed was 26 ms per frame (38 frames per second) on a mobile tablet. This organ detection algorithm identifies the key organ features and their interfaces, which are important for FF assessment. The algorithm has a low inference speed that approximates real time temporal resolution, providing a foundation for future work supporting automated image capture and quality assessment.

title: Buy the Workflow, Not the Algorithm: When Should Radiology Pay for Artificial Intelligence?
source: PubMed · AJR. American journal of roentgenology
desc: [AJR. American journal of roentgenology]
